text: The 1782-1787 Greek Catholic parish papers for Ung county (real.mtak.hu/63713) and a Mukachevo eparchy directory were not reached in the research pass. Either would turn PL-H-001 from supported to solved.

Catalogue 710997 was read in the research pass. Still wanted: the locality list inside FamilySearch catalogue 1411329, which would show whether Solymos is in the Uzhhorod series (PL-H-005), and the catalogue entry behind the older Senné volumes (PL-R-006).

From the line agents, when they have them: any house numbers, any place names written on register pages, and the archive reference on the 1869 and c. 1754 images. Each one is a test for a place hypothesis.

Exact coordinates still wanted for Palín, Stretava, Stretavka, Jastrabie pri Michalovciach, Blatná Polianka, Belá nad Cirochou, Čičarovce, Gyňov, Seňa, Valaliky and Lastomír, all placed approximately.

Still not found for Senné: the notarial and civil-registry districts, the 1913 gazetteer entry, the 1921 and 1930 census sheets online, the military survey and cadastral maps, and how the village name was spelled in passenger lists. Queued for a second pass.

Assigned by the coordinator under X-Q-01 and asked by the Demko agent: which Iňačovce Greek Catholic volumes after 1898 survive, and where. Still not answered. The Prešov state archive's catalogue ends at no. 383 (to 1898). A note of 1934 in that volume shows it outlived the fire of 1930, so the older books were not lost; the volumes begun in 1899 are not located. Next step is a written question to the parish, the Košice eparchy archive and the registry office that now serves Iňačovce. A baptism extract of 1929 for Senné cites 'tomo IV, pag. 110', which shows that parishes here kept later volumes that never reached the state archive.

Burial counts by year to turn the epidemic timeline into village evidence. The volumes are now known: Senné nos. 1091 and 1093, Iňačovce nos. 380 to 383, Viszoka in Čičarovce nos. 182 and 182/1. Needs the register images.

Not reached in the second pass: the 1715, 1720 and 1828 lists and urbarial tables for the new villages; the 1869, 1921, 1930 and 1941 census sheets; the 1877 and 1913 gazetteers; the locality list of FamilySearch catalogue 1411329; why 1890s entries were copied onto a Slovak printed form.

The last pages of the Prešov catalogue (its contents list and any introduction) were not reached, and the Topoľany entry was seen only as numbers. Not yet looked up there: Čičarovce as read by this agent, Bežovce, Lekárovce, Zemplínska Široká, and what the 'duplicate' volumes of 1882-1895 are.

Where Ung county's second copies went: of church registers under the law of 1827, and of the state registers from 1895. The inventory of the Ung county archive in the Zakarpattia archive would say. It decides between PL-H-015 and PL-H-016.
